clauses.label: operative lead
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in the President by the Constitution 
and statutes of the United States, including section 5(b)  of the act of 
October 6, 1917, as amended (12 U.S.C. 95a), and in view of the con­
tinued existence of the national emergencies declared by Proclamation 
No. 2914 of December 16, 1950, and Proclamation No. 4074 of Au­
gust 15, 1971, and the importance of continuing (a ) to exercise the 
necessary vigilance over exports from the standpoint of their significance 
to the national security of the United States; (b ) to further significantly 
the foreign policy of the United States and to aid in fulfilling its inter­
national responsibilities; and (c ) to protect the domestic economy from 
the excessive drain of scarce materials and reduce the serious inflationary 
impact of abnormal foreign demand, it is hereby ordered:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Notwithstanding the expiration of the Export Administra­
tion Act of 1969, as amended, the provisions for administration of that 
act contained in Executive Order 11533 of June 4, 1970 as continued 
in effect by Executive Order 11683 of August 29, 1972, shall continue 
in full force and effect and shall authorize the exercise and administration 
of export controls, under the authority vested in me as President of the 
United States by section 5(b)  of the act of October 6, 1917, as amended 
(12 U.S.C. 95a).

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Except to the extent another basis is provided in the second 
sentence of section 3 of this order, all rules and regulations issued by the 
Secretary of Commerce, published in title 15, chapter III, subchapter B 
of the Code of Federal Regulations, parts 368 to 399 inclusive, and all 
orders, regulations, licenses and other forms of administrative action 
issued or taken pursuant thereto, shall until amended or revoked by the 
Secretary of Commerce, remain in full force and effect, the same as if 
issued or taken pursuant to this order, except that the maximum fine 
which may be imposed under part 387.1 (a )(1 ) shall not exceed $10,000 
and that the civil penalty provided for under part 387.1 (b ) (3 ) will not 
be applicable to any violation of the regulations under this order.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. The delegations of authority in this order shall not affect the 
authority of any agency or official pursuant to any other delegation of 
Presidental authority, presently in effect or hereafter made, under section 
5 (b ) of the act of October 6,1917, as amended. Those regulations issued 
under the Export Control Act of 1949, as amended, to implement foreign 
policy set forth in Executive Orders Nos. 11322 of January 5, 1967 and 
11419 of July 29, 1968, shall until amended or revoked by the Secretary 
of Commerce continue to apply as regulations issued under such orders.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 11796 (39 FR 27891, signed July 30, 1974, Continuing the Regulation of Exports): issued under section 5(b) of the act of October 6, 1917 (12 U.S.C. 95a) because the Export Administration Act had expired, it continues EO 11533 and the export-control rules, regulations and actions in effect until amended or revoked. It has no own term. I read the held full text of EO 11798 (signed August 14, 1974), titled 'Revoking Executive Order No. 11796 of July 30, 1974, and Continuing in Effect Executive Order No. 11533': sec. 1 provides 'Executive Order No. 11796 of July 30, 1974, issued under the authority of the act of October 6, 1917, as amended (12 U.S.C. 95a), is hereby revoked, except that this revocation shall not affect any violation of any rules, regulations, orders, licenses, and other forms of administrative action under said order which occurred during the period said order was in effect.' That names EO 11796 by number and date and revokes the whole order. The savings exception preserves only liability for past violations, not the order's operation. Sec. 2 continues EO 11533 and the actions under it pursuant to Public Law 93-372, effective as of the close of July 30, 1974; that continuance rests on EO 11533 and the statute, not on EO 11796. D6 self-check: a search of the held full-run texts for '11796' finds only EO 11796 and EO 11798; no held later instrument names or restores EO 11796. The other dossier actor leads (EO 11810 of September 30, 1974 and EO 11940 of September 30, 1976, both continuing export regulation under section 5(b) of the 1917 act, and EO 11978 of 1977 on Southern Rhodesia trade) were read in the held texts; none names EO 11796. Later event on the revoking order: I read the held text of EO 12002 (signed July 7, 1977, Administration of the Export Administration Act of 1969, as amended; held as the APP transcription, no FR-original image held). Sec. 7 revokes EO 11533, EO 11683, EO 11798, EO 11818, EO 11907 and EO 11940. That revocation of EO 11798 does not revive EO 11796: EO 12002 neither names EO 11796 nor contains any revival wording, and the revocation of a revoking order does not by itself restore the order it revoked. Sec. 6 of EO 12002 keeps in force only the delegations, rules, regulations, orders, licenses and other administrative actions taken under, or continued in existence by, the revoked orders. Through EO 11798 sec. 2 that means EO 11533 and the actions under it, which EO 11798 continued under Public Law 93-372, not EO 11796; EO 11798 sec. 1 had already revoked EO 11796 outright. Sec. 6 also preserves past violations, as EO 11798 sec. 1 did. The 1977 revocation of EO 11798 therefore leaves the 1974 end of EO 11796 unchanged. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 11798, August 14, 1974' and the 1989 snapshot row (revoked, actor EO 11798) agree. Both history observations were reviewed. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing August 14, 1974) is not otherwise adjudicated.

reviews.rationale: Full independent Opus review (2026-10-20) against the held source texts, with an explicit D6 step. Accept, with defect; the NO status stands. Held EO 11796 (39 FR 27891, July 30, 1974) continues EO 11533 and the export rules under sec. 5(b) of the 1917 act after the Export Administration Act lapsed; it has no own term. Held EO 11798 (39 FR 29567, Aug. 14, 1974) sec. 1 revokes EO 11796 by number and date. Its only exception saves past violations, not the order. Sec. 2 continues EO 11533 under P.L. 93-372, not EO 11796. D6: a search of all 6,652 held full-run FR texts and the APP texts for '11796' finds only EO 11796 and EO 11798. EOs 11810, 11940 and 11978 are held and do not name EO 11796. I read held EO 12002 (July 7, 1977). Its sec. 7 revokes EO 11798, but it does not name EO 11796 and has no revival wording. Its sec. 6 keeps only actions taken under, or continued by, the revoked orders, so EO 11796 is not revived. Defect: the rationale says EO 12002 is held only as the APP transcription with no FR original. In fact an FR original is held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12002.txt (42 FR 35623-24, OCR). That text matches secs. 6 and 7 as quoted, so the conclusion is unaffected. The first end is Aug. 14, 1974.
